title: Stone Game IV
summary: Alice and Bob play a game starting with n stones.
statement: Alice and Bob play a game starting with n stones. Each turn, a player must remove a non-zero square number of stones. The player who cannot make a move loses. Determine if Alice wins given n, assuming both play optimally.
constraints: Players alternate removing a positive square number of stones.
Return whether the first player has a winning strategy under optimal play.
hints: A position is winning if any legal move leaves a losing position.
Build results from zero stones upward.
Try every square not exceeding the current pile.
All moves lead to smaller already-computed states, so the recurrence exactly represents optimal play.
editorial: All moves lead to smaller already-computed states, so the recurrence exactly represents optimal play.

tests.explanation: Remove one square stone and win immediately.
Any move leaves one stone, which the opponent removes to win.
